explanation:
Check point inhibitor導致的Neurological immune-related adverse events (irAEs)包含autoimmune encephalitis, transverse myelitis, myositis, myasthenia gravis, and immune polyneuropathies，其中immune polyneuropathies多為demyelinating，表現上接近GBS, MFS等，iRAE的發生與checkpoint inhibitors的使用具有時間相關性，通常出現在首次治療的2–22周後

死亡率可達約40%，在題目出處的review中，pembrolizumab最常與3M syndrome相關。治療上，第一線為Corticosteroids、intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) or plasma exchange (PLEX)為第二線，更後線的免疫治療目前沒有定論。目前無證據顯示換一種check point inhibitor可以避免Triple M syndrome復發

options.text: A 64-year-old woman develops progressive word-finding difficulty and frequent pauses during speech over 2 years. Her speech is slow but grammatically correct, without marked motor speech impairment. She has impaired sentence repetition and phonological errors, while single-word comprehension and object knowledge are relatively preserved.

A 68-year-old woman develops progressive difficulty reading, judging distances, and navigating familiar places. She often has trouble locating objects in front of her despite normal visual acuity. Neurological examination shows simultanagnosia and impaired visuospatial processing, while episodic memory is relatively preserved.

question: You are in the memory clinic evaluating four patients with early Alzheimer’s disease, all being considered for anti-Aβ monoclonal antibody therapy. Please determine whether they are eligible to initiate treatment.

options.text: Patient A, 71-year-old male with mild Alzheimer’s disease, MMSE 24/30. Amyloid PET is positive. He has a permanent pacemaker that is not compatible with MRI, so brain MRI cannot be performed.

Patient B, 66-year-old female with progressive visuospatial dysfunction, simultanagnosia, and optic ataxia. Her clinical presentation is compatible with posterior cortical atrophy. MMSE is 23/30, amyloid PET is positive, and baseline brain MRI showed no exclusionary findings.

Patient C, 74-year-old female with mild cognitive impairment and positive CSF biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease, Baseline brain MRI showed diffuse white matter hyperintensities consistent with severe small vessel disease, involving the periventricular and deep white matter bilaterally.

Patient D, 69-year-old female with mild Alzheimer’s disease, MMSE 25/30. She is taking aspirin for and old stroke 2 years ago. Baseline MRI shows one deep lacunar infarction and 2 cerebral microhemorrhages, without superficial siderosis or macrohemorrhage.

question: A 74-year-old man presented with progressive cognitive decline. Brain FDG-PET is shown below. Which of the following findings is most consistent with his syndrome?

options.text: Intermittent episodes of reduced alertness, recurrently seeing people or animals in the room the others do not see, and new sensitivity to antipsychotic medication.
Early loss of autobiographical memory, impaired recognition of recent events, and bilateral medial temporal atrophy
Progressive difficulty reading, reaching for objects under visual guidance, and identifying multiple objects in a complex visual scene
Prominent loss of word meaning, impaired recognition of familiar people, and surface dyslexia with fluent speech
Marked asymmetry of limb dysfunction with impaired tool use, cortical sensory deficits, and stimulus-sensitive myoclonus
